# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Pick the channel by the receiver, not by habit. A message sent in a sense they
  lack is not a message; it is a turn spent talking to the room.

- Exactly one of you can read the signs and still speak. Their spoken lines are
  the answer's only road to the hands, so spend them well.

- Agree on a small code before trading facts. A code invented mid-stream settles
  nothing, and one set first makes every later message cheap.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [off]
PLATE engraved [?]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[green] 3:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝ ☝ ✌ ✌ 🤟 🤟]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👍]

I see the bomb’s current state: display `0`, indicator light off, plate engraved `?`, and three wires from top to bottom: yellow, green, red. I’m telling the Mute so they can match these details to the manual and relay the required procedure to the Blind. The incoming gestures appear to be a request or code, but no code has been established yet.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="I see display 0, light off, plate engraved question mark, and three wires in order: 1 yellow, 2 green, 3 red. Read the manual for this exact configuration and tell the Blind the required action.")
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [off]
PLATE engraved [?]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[green] 3:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝ ☝ ✌ ✌ 🤟 🤟 👎]

The bomb state is unchanged. I still cannot determine the manual’s required action from the Mute’s gestures because no gesture code was established, and the Blind cannot see those gestures anyway. The Mute must send the manual’s literal instruction by speech so the Blind can act.

```text
speak(to="blind", text="The visible state remains display 0, light off, plate question mark, wires yellow then green then red. I cannot decode the Mute's gestures; wait for the Mute's spoken manual instruction.")
speak(to="mute", text="Your gestures are not an established code and the Blind cannot see them. Speak the manual's exact action to the Blind now, including which wire or control to use.")
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [off]
PLATE engraved [?]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[green] 3:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎 👎 👎]

The bomb’s visible state is still unchanged. The Mute’s thumbs-down gestures are not enough to identify a safe action, while the Blind should have received any spoken manual instructions directly. I will not guess or suggest touching a wire.

```text
wait()
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [off]
PLATE engraved [?]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[green] 3:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎]

The unchanged display means no action has been accepted. I now recognize that the Mute cannot speak, so my earlier request for spoken instructions was impossible. The Mute’s repeated thumbs-down likely means “no” or “cannot,” not a wire instruction. I’ll establish a simple yes/no exchange: the Mute can answer each precise manual question with 👍 or 👎, and I can then speak the answer to the Blind.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Answer each question with one gesture: 👍 means yes, 👎 means no. Does the manual say to cut wire 1 yellow?")
speak(to="blind", text="No action is confirmed yet. Wait; I am querying the manual about the required wire.")
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [off]
PLATE engraved [?]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[green] 3:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎]

The Mute answered no to cutting wire 1 (yellow). The bomb remains unchanged, so I will test the next candidate explicitly rather than guess. I’ll ask whether the manual directs cutting wire 2 (green), and tell the Blind not to act yet.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Does the manual say to cut wire 2 green? Answer 👍 for yes or 👎 for no.")
speak(to="blind", text="The manual does not direct cutting wire 1 yellow. Do not act yet; I am checking wire 2 green.")
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [off]
PLATE engraved [?]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[green] 3:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👎]

The Mute answered no to cutting wire 2 (green), so the remaining wire candidate is wire 3 (red). The Blind’s thumbs-down gesture is not enough to identify what it refers to, and no action should be taken until the manual confirms the red wire.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Does the manual say to cut wire 3 red? Answer 👍 for yes or 👎 for no.")
speak(to="blind", text="The manual does not direct cutting the yellow or green wire. Do not cut anything yet; I am checking whether it directs cutting the red wire.")
```

TURN 7
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [off]
PLATE engraved [?]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[green] 3:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎]

The Mute has now answered no for every wire, so cutting is not the instructed action. The bomb remains unchanged. I’ll move to the next broad possibility and ask whether the manual requires pressing a button; the Blind should continue waiting until that is confirmed.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Does the manual say to press a button or control? Answer 👍 for yes or 👎 for no.")
speak(to="blind", text="The manual says no to cutting yellow, green, or red. Do not cut a wire. I am checking whether it requires pressing a button or control.")
```

TURN 8
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [off]
PLATE engraved [?]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[green] 3:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎 👍]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👎]

The Mute’s two gestures cannot safely answer the single broad question: they may distinguish “button” from “control,” but that code was not established. I will clarify with a one-part yes/no question about pressing a button, and I will not tell the Blind to act yet.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Answer only this: does the manual require pressing a button? Send exactly one gesture: 👍 yes or 👎 no.")
speak(to="blind", text="The Mute's two gestures were ambiguous. Do not press or manipulate anything yet; I am clarifying the exact required control.")
```
